title: Subject-Verb Agreement
tagline: Grammar · making the verb agree with its true subject

sourceNote.boardprep: All rules, tables, example sentences, questions and answers on this page are original BoardPrep material written for practice and are not taken from any textbook, guide or past paper.

overview.intro: Subject-verb agreement means that a verb must match its subject in number: a singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb. The difficulty lies in finding the true subject when other words come between it and the verb, or when the subject is a collective noun, an uncountable noun or a pair of joined subjects. This chapter lists the rules in order and shows the traps.

facts.label: Main idea
facts.value: The verb agrees with the true subject, not with the nearest noun

facts.label: Danger zone
facts.value: Phrases between the subject and the verb

facts.label: Joined subjects
facts.value: And usually makes a plural; or and nor use the nearer subject

facts.label: Words that look plural
facts.value: News, mathematics and physics are singular

facts.label: Best habit
facts.value: Cross out the phrase between subject and verb, then check

blocks.text: In the present tense, most singular subjects take a verb ending in s (she plays, the dog barks) and plural subjects take the base form (they play, the dogs bark). With to be and to have the forms change more: is and was, are and were, has and have. To choose correctly, first find the true subject: ask who or what performs the action or is described, and ignore phrases that merely add information.

items.text: The box of pencils is on the table.
items.note: The true subject is box (singular). Pencils belongs to the phrase of pencils and does not decide the verb.

items.text: The pencils in the box are new.
items.note: Here the subject is pencils, so the verb is plural.

items.meaning: Phrases beginning with along with, together with, as well as, in addition to and besides do not change the number of the subject. The teacher, along with her students, has arrived.
Two subjects joined by and take a plural verb: Ravi and Meena are friends. If the two words name one thing or one idea, the verb is singular: Bread and butter is his usual breakfast.
The verb agrees with the subject nearer to it. Neither the manager nor the clerks were present. Neither the clerks nor the manager was present.
Each, every, either, neither, one, everyone, everybody, anyone, nobody and someone take a singular verb. Each of the players has a locker. Either of the answers is correct.

A collective noun (committee, team, family, class, jury) takes a singular verb when the group acts as one unit and a plural verb when its members act separately. The committee has decided. The committee are divided in their opinions. When in doubt, use the singular.

items.term: Rule 6. Nouns ending in s that are singular
items.meaning: News, mathematics, physics, economics, measles and politics (as a subject of study) are singular. The news is good. Mathematics is my favourite subject.
Scissors, trousers, spectacles and pliers take a plural verb. The scissors are on the shelf. With a pair of, the verb agrees with pair: A pair of scissors is on the shelf.

items.term: Rule 8. The number of and a number of
items.meaning: The number of is singular: The number of accidents has risen. A number of means several and is plural: A number of students are absent.

items.term: Rule 9. Fractions, percentages and some, all, most
items.meaning: The verb agrees with the noun after of. Half of the cake is left. Half of the mangoes are rotten.

items.term: Rule 10. Amounts of money, time and distance
items.meaning: Treated as a single unit, they take a singular verb. Ten kilometres is a long walk. Fifty rupees is enough.

items.term: Rule 11. One of, many a, more than one
items.meaning: One of the boys is late (verb agrees with one). Many a student has failed. More than one student has complained. All three take singular verbs.

items.term: Rule 12. There is and there are
items.meaning: The verb agrees with the noun that follows. There is a problem. There are several problems.

items.text: My friends ___ (be) waiting outside. Answer: are.
Every boy and girl ___ (have) a book. Answer: has.
items.note: Every before both nouns makes the subject singular.

items.text: The captain, as well as the players, ___ (be) tired. Answer: is.
items.note: As well as does not make the subject plural.

items.text: Neither the teacher nor the students ___ (know) the answer. Answer: know.
items.note: Nearer subject is students, which is plural.

items.text: The number of cars on the road ___ (increase) every year. Answer: increases.
A number of birds ___ (nest) on that tree. Answer: nest.
items.note: A number of means several, so the verb is plural.

items.text: Two-thirds of the students ___ (be) present, but two-thirds of the fee ___ (be) unpaid. Answer: are; is.
items.note: With a fraction, the verb agrees with the noun after of: students is plural, fee is singular.

learn.title: Common mistakes and how to correct them

items.text: Wrong: The quality of these mangoes are poor. Right: The quality of these mangoes is poor.
items.note: The subject is quality, not mangoes.

items.text: Wrong: The news about the floods are worrying. Right: The news about the floods is worrying.
Wrong: Each of the boys have finished. Right: Each of the boys has finished.
Wrong: The number of accidents have risen. Right: The number of accidents has risen.
Wrong: Ten kilometres are too far to walk. Right: Ten kilometres is too far to walk.
items.note: A distance is a single unit.

items.text: Wrong: Neither of the answers are right. Right: Neither of the answers is right.

items: Step 1. Find the verb and ask who or what does it.
Step 2. Cross out any phrase that begins with of, along with, as well as, together with or in addition to.
Step 3. Decide whether the true subject is singular or plural. Check for joined subjects and indefinite words such as each and neither.
Step 4. Watch sentences that begin with there or here. The subject comes after the verb.
Step 5. Match the verb to the subject and check the tense as well.
Step 6. If a sentence has been rewritten, check whether the change of subject changes the verb, for example from a child has to the children have.

keyPoints: The verb agrees with the true subject, not with the noun nearest to it.
Along with, as well as, together with and in addition to do not make a singular subject plural.
Either...or and neither...nor: the verb agrees with the nearer subject.
Each, every, either, neither, everyone and nobody take singular verbs.
News, mathematics, physics and economics are singular despite the final s.
The number of is singular; a number of is plural.
Distances, sums of money and periods of time treated as one amount take a singular verb.
In there is and there are sentences, the verb agrees with the noun that follows.
examFocus: Filling gaps with is or are, has or have, was or were, and other verb forms.
Correcting sentences in which the verb does not agree with its subject.
Spotting agreement errors in a short passage.
Rewriting a sentence with a plural subject and adjusting the verb.
Knowing the exceptions: collective nouns, indefinite pronouns, singular nouns ending in s.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: The teacher, along with her students, ___ arrived at the museum.
questions.explanation: The true subject is teacher (singular). Along with her students is an added phrase and does not change the number.
questions.commonMistake: Choosing have because students is plural.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: Neither the manager nor the clerks ___ present at the meeting.
questions.explanation: With neither...nor, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, clerks, which is plural.
questions.commonMistake: Agreeing the verb with the first subject.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: Mathematics ___ my favourite subject.
questions.explanation: Mathematics names a single subject of study and takes a singular verb despite the final s.
questions.commonMistake: Treating a noun ending in s as plural.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct option: A number of students ___ absent today.
questions.explanation: A number of means several and takes a plural verb. Compare: The number of students is small.
questions.commonMistake: Mixing up a number of and the number of.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with has or have: Each of the players ___ a locker in the sports room.
questions.explanation: Each is singular, even though players is plural.
questions.commonMistake: Writing have because players is nearer the verb.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with is or are: There ___ several mistakes in your answer.
questions.explanation: In a sentence beginning with there, the verb agrees with the noun that follows: mistakes is plural.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with is or are: Bread and butter ___ his usual breakfast.
questions.answer: is (Bread and butter is his usual breakfast.)
questions.explanation: Bread and butter is thought of as one combined food, so the verb is singular. This is an exception to the usual rule that two subjects joined by and take a plural verb.
questions.commonMistake: Treating every and-joined pair as plural.

questions.prompt: Correct the verb in this sentence: The quality of these mangoes are poor.
questions.answer: The quality of these mangoes is poor.
questions.explanation: The true subject is quality (singular). These mangoes belongs to the phrase of these mangoes.
questions.commonMistake: Letting the noun nearest the verb decide the agreement.

questions.prompt: Rewrite the sentence with a plural subject and make all necessary changes: The child has finished his lunch and is playing in the garden.
questions.answer: The children have finished their lunch and are playing in the garden.
questions.explanation: Child becomes children, has becomes have, his becomes their and is becomes are.
questions.commonMistake: Changing the noun but forgetting the pronoun or the second verb.

questions.prompt: Explain why the verb is singular in 'The captain, as well as the players, is tired', and rewrite the sentence using and so that the verb changes.
questions.answer: The subject is captain, which is singular. As well as the players is an extra phrase and does not join the subjects, so the verb stays singular. With and the subject becomes plural: The captain and the players are tired.
questions.explanation: The answer needs the rule about added phrases and a correct rewrite with the verb changed to are.
questions.commonMistake: Thinking that as well as works exactly like and.

questions.prompt: Each sentence has one agreement error. Rewrite it correctly. (a) Ten kilometres are too far to walk. (b) Either of the answers are correct. (c) The number of accidents have risen. (d) Many a student have failed the test.
questions.answer: (a) Ten kilometres is too far to walk. (b) Either of the answers is correct. (c) The number of accidents has risen. (d) Many a student has failed the test.
questions.explanation: (a) A distance is one unit. (b) Either is singular. (c) The number of is singular. (d) Many a is followed by a singular noun and a singular verb.
questions.commonMistake: Correcting the verb to agree with the last noun in the sentence instead of the true subject.

questions.prompt: Both 'The committee has decided to postpone the event' and 'The committee are divided in their opinions' are acceptable. Explain why the verb differs, and say which form is safer if you are not sure.
questions.answer: A collective noun takes a singular verb when the group acts as one unit, as in the first sentence where the committee makes one decision. It takes a plural verb when the members are thought of as individuals with different views, as in the second sentence. The singular is the safer choice when in doubt.
questions.explanation: The plural use of a collective noun is common in British English when the members act separately. Full credit for stating the unit-versus-individuals idea and the safer choice.
questions.commonMistake: Believing that one of the two sentences must be wrong.
